title: Hemoglobin Test
text: Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body. A hemoglobin test measures how much of it is in the blood. Results below or above the reference range can have many different causes, so they are best interpreted by a healthcare professional together with other tests.

title: Hematocrit Test
text: Hematocrit is the percentage of the blood volume made up of red blood cells. It is usually read together with hemoglobin and the red blood cell count.

title: Blood Glucose Test
text: A blood glucose test measures the amount of sugar (glucose) in the blood. The result depends on factors such as whether you have recently eaten, which is why reports often state if the sample was fasting or random.

title: Cholesterol Levels
text: Cholesterol tests measure fats in the blood, usually total cholesterol, LDL, HDL and triglycerides. They are used to estimate heart and blood-vessel risk together with other factors, and a doctor interprets them in context.

title: Triglycerides Test
text: Triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood. The test is often part of a lipid panel.

title: Creatinine Test
text: Creatinine is a waste product made by muscles and removed by the kidneys. Blood creatinine is used as one way to check how well the kidneys are working.

title: BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen) Test
text: Urea nitrogen is a waste product the kidneys remove from the blood. The test is used, along with other tests such as creatinine, to look at kidney function.

title: Bilirubin Blood Test
text: Bilirubin is a yellow substance made when red blood cells break down. The liver removes it from the body. The test is used to learn about liver and bile-duct function.

title: Calcium Blood Test
text: Calcium is a mineral important for bones, nerves, muscles and the heart. The blood test measures how much calcium is in the blood.

title: Platelet Tests
text: Platelets are blood cell fragments that help blood clot. A platelet count shows how many are in the blood.

title: White Blood Count (WBC)
text: White blood cells are part of the immune system. A WBC count measures how many are in the blood; a differential shows the share of each type (such as neutrophils and lymphocytes).

title: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
text: A complete blood count measures several parts of the blood, including red cells, white cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit and platelets. Indices such as MCV, MCH and MCHC describe the size and hemoglobin content of red blood cells.

title: Sodium Blood Test
text: Sodium is an electrolyte that helps control fluid balance and nerve and muscle function.

title: Potassium Blood Test
text: Potassium is an electrolyte needed for normal nerve, muscle and heart function.

title: Ferritin Blood Test
text: Ferritin is a protein that stores iron. The test is used to estimate how much iron the body has stored.

title: Vitamin D Test
text: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for healthy bones. The blood test measures the amount of vitamin D in the body.

title: ALT Blood Test
text: ALT is an enzyme found mostly in the liver. It is one of the liver function tests.

title: Liver Function Tests
text: Liver function tests measure enzymes, proteins and bilirubin in the blood to see how well the liver is working.

title: Uric Acid Test
text: Uric acid is a waste product made when the body breaks down substances called purines. The test measures how much is in the blood.
